## What Is a Founding Engineer?


A founding engineer is your technical co-founder without the formal title. They’re the first engineering hire who takes ownership of building your product from the ground up, implementing features and creating the foundation.


In AI startups, founding engineers wear multiple hats as they help:


-


Architect your initial tech stack


-


Contribute to product strategy based on what’s technically feasible


Founding engineers often help with technical hiring as you scale, represent your company at conferences, and help with bridging your vision and technical reality.


For AI startups, this role is even more important because the tech scene changes every minute. Your founding engineer needs to stay updated with the latest developments in[AI engineering](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-hire-ai-engineers-startups) , while building production-ready systems that can scale.


## Why Hiring a Founding Engineer Matters for AI Startups


AI startups are constantly working with challenges like rapidly evolving tech, managing complex model deployments, and often dealing with major computational costs from day one.


They make choices that have massive implications for your burn rate and technical debt. A founding engineer can help you:


-


Avoid costly architectural mistakes: They should understand the tradeoffs between different AI approaches and decide whether to build custom models, fine-tune existing ones, or use APIs.


-


Achieve product-market fit: They can quickly prototype new features, experiment with different model approaches, and help you iterate based on user feedback


-


Fundraise: VCs want to see that you have someone who can handle the complexities of AI development and scale your technology as you grow.


The talent market for AI engineers is incredibly competitive right now. Companies like[OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google](https://www.dw.com/en/ai-superintelligence-meta-lab-companies-are-going-after-top-programmers/a-73392978) are paying top dollar for experienced AI talent. Having a founding engineer who’s invested in your success through equity gives you a major advantage in building your initial team.


## What to Look for in an AI Founding Engineer


Technical expertise is obviously important, but the specific skills matter. Look for candidates with:


-


Hands-on experience building various production AI systems


-


Experience with the full stack over deep specialization


-


Understanding to articulate technical tradeoffs and it’s impact


-


Cultural fit and adaptability to startup environment


Most importantly, find someone who’s ready to trade stability for the opportunity to build something from scratch.

## How to Assess and Screen Candidates


Looking at founding engineer candidates requires a different approach than hiring for existing engineering teams. You need to assess both technical competency and their ability to thrive in fast-moving environment. During assessment, focus on:


-


Technical screening test with AI/ML: Ask them to walk through a complex system they’ve built and explain the technical decisions they made.


-


Architectural thinking: Pay attention to how they communicate technical concepts and whether they consider business constraints in their technical choices.


-


Cultural fit: They need to be comfortable making decisions and adapt to evolving needs. Ask about times they’ve had to pivot technical approaches or work with limited resources.


-


Reference checks: Speak with previous managers and colleagues about their technical leadership, and how they handle pressure.


-


Involving technical advisors or investors: They help you get additional perspective on candidates’ technical depth and avoid blind spots in your evaluation.


Bonus Tip: For the technical interview, consider giving candidates a realistic problem similar to what they’d face in your startup. Skip abstract coding challenges, and present them with a scenario like “design a system to fine-tune and deploy a custom LLM for our use case.”


This reveals their practical experience and problem-solving approach.


## How to Structure Compensation for Founding Engineers


Compensation for founding engineers typically combines competitive base salary with meaningful equity upside.[Bureau of Labor Statistics software developer wages](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/software-developers.htm) exceeded $130,000 annually in recent surveys, and AI-focused engineers typically command a premium above that. In the current market, expect to pay between $120k-200k in base salary, supported by[founding engineer salary benchmarks](https://topstartups.io/startup-salary-equity-database/?title=Founding%20software%20engineer) at early-stage companies, with equity grants ranging from 2-5% of the company.


You need to understand what the potential candidate values the most. Some prefer equity component more than the base salary as they’re taking major risk by joining an early-stage company.


While some prefer non-monetary aspect, where they are more excited about having clear paths to technical leadership, and opportunities to shape company culture. So based on candidate:


-


Discuss the learning opportunities and impact if the focus is on leadership


-


Performance-based equity grants based on technical milestones or company growth metrics


-


Offer mix of stock options and restricted stock to balance immediate ownership with long-term incentives


Be transparent about your funding situation and runway. Founding engineers need to understand the financial stability of the company and your future fundraising plans.

## How to Close and Onboard Founding Engineers


Closing top founding engineer candidates often comes down to handling their concerns about joining an early-stage company. To close founding engineers successfully, make sure to:


1.


Talk about unique opportunity your startup provides: Founding engineers want to build something from scratch, and have technical influence. Show how their contributions will directly impact company success.


2.


Handle common concerns proactively: Candidates worry about technical resources, team quality, and company stability. Be prepared to discuss your technical roadmap, hiring plans, and fundraising timeline.


The onboarding process for founding engineers should focus on context-setting rather than traditional orientation. They need to understand your vision, target market, and technical constraints.


-


Spend time explaining the problem you’re solving


-


Set clear expectations related to goals for their first 90 days


-


Provide mentorship by pairing new founding engineers with technical advisors or board members


A founding member with clear goals and external perspective can work through the challenges of startup environment easily and start faster.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What’s the difference between hiring a founding engineer versus senior engineer?


Founding engineers take ownership of building your product from scratch and make architectural decisions that impact your company long-term. While senior engineers typically implement features within existing systems.


### How much equity should I offer a founding engineer?


Expect to offer 1-5% equity depending on experience level and how early they join. Senior engineers (5-8 years) typically receive 2-4%, while principal-level engineers (12+ years) may be worth 4-6% or more, combined with competitive base salaries ranging from $140k-220k.


### What hiring tools do most YC startups use to recruit engineers?


Early-stage YC startups typically pair an ATS with direct sourcing. Ashby is popular at the seed and Series A stage for its automation and analytics, while Greenhouse and Lever suit teams of 20+ that need structured workflows. Workable works well for leaner setups. Dover is used by over 100 YC companies, combining a free ATS with on-demand fractional recruiters. For founding engineer searches, most founders skip job boards and rely on direct outreach instead, since passive candidates at top AI companies rarely apply through standard postings.
